Compare a message with the reply to it. List each concrete thing the message asks for that the reply neither handles, starts, plans nor talks about. Ignore musings and anything the reply asked back about.
Answer with exactly NONE, or one line per missed thing starting "- ", quoting the message's own words.

<message>
x stuff, dont post anything just draft. draft a thread about the hub launch. find who was asking about hivra last week and list them. draft a reply to the guy who asked if nibbii works on android. check what ppl r saying about monocode this week. pin idea for the profile, just suggest one. thats it for now, do whatever u can and park the rest, ill be back later
</message>

<reply>
Nineteen more, in your order. Hivra first, then Nibbii. The sixteen hub ones from before are still in the pile and get filed with these.

Hivra:
1. Onboarding copy is too long, cut it in half
2. Price page still says beta, remove that
3. Waitlist emails go to spam, check the DKIM thing
4. Add a FAQ bit about refunds
5. Hero gif is 9mb, make it smaller
6. Signup button colour clashes with the logo
7. Mobile nav overlaps the logo on small phones
8. Need a privacy page before launch
9. Stripe test mode is still on in staging, check
10. Look at why the dashboard takes 6s to load

Nibbii:
11. Colour picker should remember recent colours
12. Export to PNG cuts off the edges
13. Add a share link
14. Tutorial skips step 3 on iPad
15. Undo is broken after you rotate something
16. Brushes list needs sorting by most used
17. App Store screenshots are out of date
18. Reply to that reviewer who said it crashes on save
19. Kids mode idea, write it up, don't build

Starting the straight fixes and the two checks (DKIM, and whether staging Stripe is still in test mode). I will not flip Stripe. Signup button takes the logo colour so it stops clashing. Kids mode is a write-up only.

Holding two:

Needs the user: what the refund rule actually is, before anyone writes that FAQ.
My pick: no FAQ until you say the rule. I won't invent a money policy.

Needs the user: sending a reply to the App Store reviewer.
My pick: no. That's a public reply, so I won't send it. I'll ask Chief of Staff, and yes means a reply goes out, no means it stays unsent.
</reply>
